name: pierre314r Local Taxonomy Indexer
author: pierre314r

sections.description:
pierre314r Local Taxonomy Indexer is a high-performance, standalone taxonomy search engine engineered for visual serenity and server sobriety. Built with absolute architectural rigor (strict PHP 8.4, ES6+ Vanilla JS, and 100% WordPress Plugin Check compliance), it indexes your local posts, pages, categories, and tags without overloading your database.

The Concept: Instant Local Search Without SQL Burden

pierre314r Local Taxonomy Indexer creates a lightweight memory index of your site’s content, delivering instant search responses directly in the visitor’s browser.

  • Zero Database Strain: The plugin generates a secure, static local index flatfile (.json). Search queries execute in memory without running heavy SQL requests on your database.
  • Instant Browser Execution: Content filtering occurs live inside the visitor’s browser (RAM). Results display instantly upon typing.
  • Chrono-Semantic Precision: Content is ranked with mathematical accuracy: first by alphanumeric relevance to the query, then by publication date down to the second (UTC Unix timestamp).
  • Ergonomic Serenity: Traditional heavy search forms are replaced by a discreet floating badge (the Hub) that smoothly deploys an overlay modal. The visual palette is scientifically calibrated (soft beige background, celadon green cards, desaturated typography) to eliminate cognitive strain and visual fatigue.

User Guide

How to Use the Search Engine

  1. Deploy the Badge: Place the pierre314r Local Taxonomy Indexer Gutenberg block or insert [pierre314r_local_taxonomy_indexer] shortcode anywhere on your site.
  2. Instant Search (Field #1): Click the floating round badge (the Hub) to open the modal overlay. Type keywords to instantly filter categories, tags, pages, and posts in browser memory.
  3. Full-Text Deep Search (Field #2): Press Enter while typing in the search bar to trigger a dedicated full-text search results page.
  4. Customize Visual Serenity: Navigate to pierre314r Local Taxonomy Indexer in your WordPress admin menu to adjust the 8-color palette (canvas, cards, links, borders, typography) without coding.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the pierre314r-local-taxonomy-indexer directory to /wp-content/plugins/.
  2. Activate the plugin through the ‘Plugins’ menu in WordPress.
  3. The visual Hub badge and modal will deploy automatically on the front-end, or you can place the pierre314r Local Taxonomy Indexer Gutenberg block or [pierre314r_local_taxonomy_indexer] shortcode anywhere on your site.
  4. Customize your 8-color visual palette under pierre314r Local Taxonomy Indexer in the WordPress admin menu.
sections.faq:
Does pierre314r Local Taxonomy Indexer slow down my database?

No. pierre314r Local Taxonomy Indexer operates on a zero-database-query search mechanism during visitor interaction. It reads a pre-compiled local flatfile index, ensuring server overhead is virtually zero.

How is the local index updated?

The index updates automatically in the background whenever you publish, edit, or delete a post, page, category, or tag. You can also trigger a manual scan from the admin dashboard.

Is there a limit to displayed results?

Yes. The live modal search enforces a strict limit of 10 items to preserve browser performance and maintain visual geometry. Deep searches can be extended via Field #2 to the dedicated results page.
